newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian central bank buys, sells bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russian central bank buys, sells bonds.

text.p: The central bank bought 3.54 trillion roubles worth of tax-exempt OFZ government bonds and sold 3.85 trillion roubles of tax-liable bonds on behalf of the Finance Ministry in an extraordinary session on Wednesday, the bank's open-market operations department said.
The bank made the following transactions:

The central bank held a trading session today to channel money investors received from tax-exempt series 24008 bonds which were repaid on a voluntary basis. The bank has discontinued tax-exempt issues.
Banks could buy tax-liable OFZ interest-bearing bonds from the central bank but could not trade between themselves.
The total series 24008 issue volume in circulation was 4.81 trillion roubles nominal value before the sale.
The central bank does not usually hold trading sessions on Wednesdays, when auctions take place.
Today banks bid at the average Tuesday price for series 24011, 24013 and 24014 issues and at the average price for issue 24015 set at an auction on Wednesday.

The central bank did not say at what price the paper was bought or sold. The 24011 issue closed on Tuesday at 26.04 percent, the 24013 issue closed at 23.61 percent, the 24014 issue closed at 23.23 and the 24008 issue closed at 14.78 percent. The 24015 issue was priced at 97.02 percent at the auction.

Apart from intervening on its own account for liquidity-smoothing and monetary policy purposes, the central bank buys and sells securities as part of its management of the Finance Ministry's debt and asset portfolio.
